newsitem.title: UK: Brazil features in new sugar freight business.
newsitem.headline: Brazil features in new sugar freight business.

text.p: South Brazilian ports once again dominated the London sugar freight market on Wednesday, shipbrokers said.
Cargill fixed 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua or Santos to Baltic/Mediterranean/Black Sea for end July/early August.
Shipbrokers said South Africa Sugar Association fixed 14,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to the Black Sea for early August.
E D & F Man fixed 13,500/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to Lagos at a rate believed to be in the low $30 bracket.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS) was also active in the day's business, fixing an earlier inquiry for bulk sugar and launching two others.

MSS fixed 18,000 tonnes on its usual run from Port Louis to London for early August and quoted for a 14,000-tonne cargo for mid-August. It was also in the market for around 20,000 tonnes to US Gulf/Atlantic for August 5/10.

Of the day's other new business, Louis Dreyfus quoted for 13,000 tonnes in bags from Paranagua to west Africa for early August and SIMAB quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to Lagos for similar dates.
